TIP 1: Revenue accounting concern at Pelham Analytics
CHANNEL: encrypted email
RECEIVED: 04 May 2026

I am a senior revenue accountant at Pelham Analytics. Since Q1 2026, the controller's team has been booking subscription revenue into the closing quarter based on "early-start" clauses even when the customer signature arrived after quarter end.

The largest examples I reviewed were the Northstar Foods renewal signed by the customer on 04 April 2026 but recognized effective 28 March 2026, and the Cadence Mutual expansion signed on 03 July 2026 but recognized effective 29 June 2026. Together those two deals added $5.7 million to the prior quarter.

I have the ASC 606 memo drafted by Assistant Controller Mira Shah, the Salesforce opportunity history, and the revenue schedule exported from NetSuite on 08 July 2026. Shah told me the policy came from CFO Grant Ellery after the Q1 forecast missed guidance.

The policy memo does not say "backdate," but it treats the contractual start date as controlling even when execution happens later and service access is not provisioned. In the Northstar file, customer access was not enabled until 08 April according to the Okta provisioning log. For Cadence, the implementation kickoff did not occur until 09 July. Those facts were not included in the revenue memo.

I raised the Northstar issue during the April close meeting because the order form had not been signed by quarter end. Ellery said the early-start clause gave us enough support and that auditors would not sample a renewal if the paperwork was complete. I am not a securities lawyer, but I know the accounting file does not reflect when the customers actually committed or received service.

TIP 2: DealDesk pressure to backdate starts at Pelham
CHANNEL: secure drop
RECEIVED: 05 May 2026

I work in DealDesk at Pelham Analytics. During the final week of Q1 and Q2 2026, sales leadership pushed us to add early-start language to enterprise contracts after commercial terms had already been agreed.

For Northstar Foods, VP Sales Kellan Rusk posted in the DealDesk Slack channel on 30 March 2026: "Need start date inside Q1 or finance won't count it." The customer did not countersign until 04 April. For Cadence Mutual, the redline history shows the start date changed from 01 July to 29 June on the morning of 30 June.

I have the Ironclad redlines, the DealDesk Slack export, and the approval workflow showing CFO Grant Ellery approved both exceptions. I am not on the accounting team, but the requests were explicitly about quarter revenue treatment.

The same pattern showed up in smaller deals too. In the final two days of Q2, DealDesk received a spreadsheet titled `Q2 saves` with eight opportunities marked "start date help needed." The spreadsheet came from Rusk's operations manager and listed expected revenue contribution next to each account. Three of those accounts had legal comments saying the customer would not sign until July.

I pushed back once because DealDesk is supposed to document commercial terms, not solve accounting shortfalls. My manager told me the language had been approved by finance and legal, and that my job was to route the exception cleanly. I can provide the Slack export and the Ironclad version history showing when the start-date language was inserted.

TIP 3: Account executive asked to make quarter-end math work
CHANNEL: intake form
RECEIVED: 06 May 2026

I left Pelham Analytics in April 2026 after refusing to keep pushing contract language I thought was misleading. I was the account executive on the Northstar Foods renewal.

Northstar agreed to pricing on 27 March 2026 but told us procurement could not sign until the following week. On 30 March, VP Sales Kellan Rusk told me by phone that "Grant needs this in Q1" and instructed me to accept an early-start clause even though implementation would not begin until 08 April. The final countersignature came on 04 April.

I retained my call notes, the customer email from Northstar procurement, and the final order form. I do not know how finance booked the deal, but the pressure was specifically to make the quarter's math work before the earnings call.

Northstar's procurement manager, Ellie Baird, was explicit that their approval committee would not meet until 02 April. I forwarded that email to Rusk and asked whether we should forecast the renewal for Q2. He called me instead of replying in writing and said the CFO was "personally watching" the deal. After the call, Rusk sent a one-line Slack message: "Use the early start, paper follows."

I left because this was becoming normal. The same instruction came up on a smaller contract with FleetRiver Manufacturing, though that one closed before quarter end. I cannot prove the accounting entry from my sales records alone, but my records show the customer did not commit by 31 March and management still pushed contract language designed to place the deal inside Q1.
